headline: Every bag of seed checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: With different crops and varieties going through cleaning and bagging, every bag needs the right label and lot code. Here's what a camera check could look like after your bagger. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every bag is closed straight across, with no open corners or split tops. A bag that opens in the truck means lost seed and a call from the grower.
labelLede: Seed for different crops and varieties looks the same in the bag. The camera checks every bag carries the right label for the seed inside, straight and intact.
codeLede: The lot code is how a bag is traced back to its cleaning run and seed test. The system reads the printed lot code on every bag and compares it with the lot set at changeover.
objectLede: String, bag offcuts and pallet splinters can all end up on the bag conveyor. The camera spots anything that should not be there before bags are stacked.

vocab.alert: Four crooked closures in fifteen minutes. Check the bag closer.
